title: Attempt record (one JSONL line per graded item)
description: The only source of truth for how the learner is actually doing. Progress reports are computed from these rows, never from the tutor's impression.

concept_results.description: One independent result for each concept on a multi-concept item. Historical attempts without this field remain readable, but new multi-concept attempts cannot be recorded without it. A wrong part must not lower an unrelated concept.

tier.description: Exercise difficulty tier. Absent for a probe or an explain-back, which are not exercises.

graded_by.description: script:<grader name>, agent:zt-grader, or manual. The teaching persona never appears here.

verdict.description: unassessed means the submitted work was not reliably judged, for example when a valid alternative route is outside the rubric or the input was unreadable. Keep the answer without changing mastery.

evidence_quotes.description: NO-LENIENCY RULE. A pass verdict must quote the specific lines in the learner answer that earned it. If nothing can be quoted, the verdict is not a pass. Enforced by semantic validation, not by prompt.

grader_raw_path.description: Path to raw grader output or run log, kept for audit.

where.description: Free text, in the learner's words: where this was actually carried out. The plugin holds no list of kinds of place.

degraded.description: True when the exercise ran in a fallback form because a capability was missing.

latency_rating.description: How hard the recall was, not just whether it landed. Main input to the next review interval.

latency_source.description: Zep infers this by default and says so out loud; the learner can overrule it, which is recorded as learner_corrected.

depth_demonstrated.description: What depth this item actually proved: 1 can-use, 2 can-compute, 3 can-derive, 4 can-critique, 5 can-create. Without it the depth ceiling cannot be enforced, because nothing says how deep the learner went.

interleaved.description: True when the item came from a mixed drill where the prompt did not reveal which method applies.

transfer_dimensions.description: Copied from the item. Without it, a recorded transfer pass is an unfalsifiable claim about what the learner can now do.

answer.description: What the learner actually submitted, kept verbatim. Stored because for a while it was not: the answer lived in the conversation, the verdict lived on disk, and the two could not be checked against each other afterwards. A learner reading their own records could see that something was marked wrong without being able to see what they wrote.

response_values.description: The same answer as data, keyed by the item's response field ids (or option ids for a choice). Present whenever the item named its slots. This is what makes an answer comparable to the next attempt at the same item instead of being a paragraph somebody has to read.

slips.description: Points where the answer went wrong in execution rather than in understanding - an arithmetic error, a transcription error, a sign dropped - which the learner's reasoning elsewhere in the same answer shows they can do correctly. Recorded separately from failure_points because merging the two is a real failure this system produced: three consecutive retests of one concept the learner understood, driven by a slip each time, ending with them writing that the concepts were clear and the mistakes were arithmetic.

execution_only.description: True when every criterion about the idea was met and the only unmet ones were about carrying it out. Computed by grade.py from the rubric, not asserted. A concept is not moved backwards by one of these: the evidence it gives about the concept is positive, and the thing that went wrong is worth a redo of that step rather than a retest of the idea.
